title: Pullback naturality of the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $X,Y$ be schemes of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], let $u:X\to Y$ be a morphism, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient sheaves $A_X,A_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the derived module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with the canonical identification $u^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For $T=X,Y$, let $F_T:T\to T$ be absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] and let
$$
\tau_T^{(b)}:L(F_T^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)},\qquad b\geq0,
$$
be the canonical trivialization induced by the relative Frobenius isomorphisms $r_{V/T}^{(b)}=(F_V^b,v):V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_{T,F_T^b}T$ for weakly etale objects $v:V\to T$: restriction along these isomorphisms identifies direct image by $F_T^b$ with the identity, the adjoint identification gives the inverse-image trivialization of module sheaves (the coefficient identification being that of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]), and the inverse image being exact, it induces $\tau_T^{(b)}$ termwise on complexes. For $b=1$ this specifies the canonical trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]; $\tau_T^{(0)}$ is the identity.

Using the canonical composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], the equality $uF_X^b=F_Y^bu$ gives the pullback-composition identification
$$
 c_{u,b}:Lu^*L(F_Y^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(F_X^b)^*Lu^*.
$$
As natural transformations on $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ one has
$$
 (\tau_X^{(b)}Lu^*)\circ c_{u,b}=Lu^*\tau_Y^{(b)}.
$$
Moreover, for integers $b_1,b_2\geq0$ and $T=X,Y$, the trivialization $\tau_T^{(b_1+b_2)}$ equals the composite
$$
 L(F_T^{b_1+b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(F_T^{b_1})^*L(F_T^{b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\tau_T^{(b_1)}L(F_T^{b_2})^*}L(F_T^{b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\tau_T^{(b_2)}}\operatorname{id},
$$
whose first arrow is the composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $F_T^{b_1+b_2}=F_T^{b_2}\circ F_T^{b_1}$; in particular $\tau_T^{(b)}$ is the $b$-fold iterate of $\tau_T^{(1)}$.

proof.text: Write $B_h(V)=V\times_{S,h}T$ for base change along $h:T\to S$, with its projection to $T$, as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. An equality of maps into a fibre product is checked on its two projections, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any characteristic-$p$ scheme map $h:T\to S$, its maps on sections satisfy $h^\sharp(a^{p^b})=h^\sharp(a)^{p^b}$; the underlying maps of both Frobenii are identities. Thus $hF_T^b=F_S^bh$, using [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. In particular $r_{V/T}^{(b)}=(F_V^b,v)$ is defined. For $b=1$, the explicit geometric assertion in the statement of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] is precisely Stacks Tag 0F6W: relative Frobenius of a weakly etale object is an isomorphism. Every scheme over a characteristic-$p$ scheme is itself of characteristic $p$, since each structure ring map sends $p\cdot1=0$ to $p\cdot1=0$. For general $b$, start with $r^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}$ under $B_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$ and compose $r_V^{(b)}$ with $r_{B_{F_T^b}V}^{(1)}$. The latter is an isomorphism because $B_{F_T^b}V$ remains a weakly etale site object by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The base-change identification $B_{F_T}B_{F_T^b}\cong B_{F_T^{b+1}}$ keeps the outermost projections; the composite has projections $F_V^{b+1}$ and $v$, hence is exactly $r^{(b+1)}$. This proves by induction that every $r^{(b)}$ is an isomorphism. For a site arrow $a:V\to V'$, both $B_{F_T^b}(a)r_V^{(b)}$ and $r_{V'}^{(b)}a$ have projections $aF_V^b=F_{V'}^ba$ and $v$, so are equal. This is naturality in the site object, not a Cartesian assertion about $u$.

proof.text: Put $H_T^{(b)}=(F_T^b)_*$ on $A_T$-module sheaves. By the direct-image formula and module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], its value on a sheaf $M$ at $V$ is $M(B_{F_T^b}V)$. Restriction defines a natural isomorphism $d_{T,M}^{(b)}:H_T^{(b)}M\to M$, whose component is $M(r_{V/T}^{(b)})$. Step 1 proves compatibility with every restriction, and functoriality of $M$ proves naturality in $M$. These are $A_T$-linear maps: the constant-coefficient structure map of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] preserves each constant section, as does restriction along $r$; locally every coefficient section is a constant, so the actions agree. The same argument shows that the coefficient identifications for a composite of scheme maps equal the composites of the coefficient identifications: their adjuncts send every constant $a$ to the constant $a$, and the constant sheaf is the sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $P_T^{(b)}=(F_T^b)^*$ on module sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $P_T^{(b)}\dashv H_T^{(b)}$ and the identity adjunction, with right-adjoint isomorphism $(d_T^{(b)})^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to H_T^{(b)}$. It gives $s_T^{(b)}:P_T^{(b)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$, characterized by $H_T^{(b)}(s_{T,N}^{(b)})\eta_N=(d_{T,N}^{(b)})^{-1}$. This fixes the direction of the adjoint trivialization in the statement; for $b=0$ it is the identity under the identity-pullback identification.

proof.text: For a site object $v:V\to Y$, set $W=B_uV=V\times_YX$, with projections $\pi_V,\pi_X$. There is a canonical isomorphism $j_V:B_{F_X^b}(B_uV)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_u(B_{F_Y^b}V)$: both fibre products are identified with $V\times_{Y,F_Y^bu}X$. In test-scheme coordinates it takes $((z,x_0),x)$, where $x_0=F_X^b(x)$, to $((z,u(x)),x)$. Its inverse inserts $x_0=F_X^b(x)$. The two maps $j_Vr_{W/X}^{(b)}$ and $B_u(r_{V/Y}^{(b)})$ from $W$ to $B_uB_{F_Y^b}V$ have the same $V$-projection $F_V^b\pi_V$ and $X$-projection $\pi_X$. Here $F_W^b$ has projections $F_V^b\pi_V,F_X^b\pi_X$ by Step 1. The fibre-product uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore gives $j_Vr_{W/X}^{(b)}=B_u(r_{V/Y}^{(b)})$. This equality holds on morphisms of schemes, including their structure-sheaf maps. Using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], restriction along $j_V^{-1}$ gives the canonical isomorphism $e:u_*H_X^{(b)}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Y^{(b)}u_*$. Contravariance of sections applied to the displayed equality gives $d_Y^{(b)}u_*\circ e=u_*d_X^{(b)}$. All maps are module maps by Step 2.

proof.text: Write $L=u^*$, $R=u_*$, $P=P_Y^{(b)}$, $Q=H_Y^{(b)}$, $S=P_X^{(b)}$, and $T=H_X^{(b)}$. The composite adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] are $LP\dashv QR$ and $SL\dashv RT$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $e:RT\cong QR$ gives the canonical comparison $c^0:LP\cong SL$. To check that this is the ordinary pullback-composition identification, use the inverse-image presentation in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For any scheme map $h$ and site object $V$ on its target, the unit sends $m\in N(V)$ to the sheafified colimit class indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{B_hV})$, with value $m$. For composable $h,k$, the iterated unit sends $m$ to the nested class indexed first by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{B_kV})$ and then by $(B_kV,\mathrm{id}_{B_hB_kV})$. Under $B_hB_kV\cong B_{kh}V$, flattening the two identity indices gives exactly the single class indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{B_{kh}V})$. Thus the ordinary inverse-image composition comparison carries the composite unit to the direct unit. Applying this to the two factorizations $uF_X^b=F_Y^bu$ gives on right adjoints exactly restriction along $j_V^{-1}$, namely $e$. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] therefore identifies its left-adjoint comparison with $c^0$. In the inverse-image/tensor presentation of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the composition map inserts a unit, $m\otimes a\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes a$; its inverse multiplies the middle scalar into $a$. Tensor balancing proves the two composites are identities. Step 2 ensures that both routes use the same coefficient map. Thus this is the termwise canonical map specifying the derived comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. To verify the required equality without assuming a mate-pasting theorem, fix $N$ on $Y$, $M$ on $X$ and $a:LN\to M$, with adjunct $a^\#:N\to RM$. Write $\eta^L,\eta^P,\eta^S$ for the units of $L\dashv R$, $P\dashv Q$, $S\dashv T$, so $a^\#=R(a)\eta^L_N$. The first adjunct, under $LP\dashv QR$, is $QR(a\circ Ls_{Y,N}^{(b)})Q(\eta^L_{PN})\eta^P_N=Q(a^\#)Q(s_{Y,N}^{(b)})\eta^P_N=Q(a^\#)(d_{Y,N}^{(b)})^{-1}=(d_{Y,RM}^{(b)})^{-1}a^\#$: the first equality uses naturality of $\eta^L$, the second the unit equation of Step 2, and the third naturality of $d_Y^{-1}$. For the second adjunct, first use $SL\dashv RT$. The $S$-adjunct of $a\circ s_{X,LN}^{(b)}$ is $T(a)T(s_{X,LN}^{(b)})\eta^S_{LN}=T(a)(d_{X,LN}^{(b)})^{-1}=(d_{X,M}^{(b)})^{-1}a$. Applying the $L$-adjunction gives $R((d_{X,M}^{(b)})^{-1})a^\#$. Finally precomposition with $c^0$ changes this adjunct by $e_M$, by the defining unit equation for $c^0$ and naturality of $e$. Thus the second adjunct is $e_M\circ R((d_X^{(b)})^{-1}_M)\circ a^\#$. Step 3, inverted, says $e_M R((d_X^{(b)})^{-1}_M)=(d_Y^{(b)})^{-1}_{RM}$. These adjuncts agree. Taking $M=LN$ and $a=\mathrm{id}$ and using injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $(s_X^{(b)}L)c^0=Ls_Y^{(b)}$ on module sheaves.

proof.text: For $b_1,b_2\geq0$, identify $B_{F_T^{b_1}}B_{F_T^{b_2}}V$ with $B_{F_T^{b_1+b_2}}V$ by keeping its $V$-projection and its last $T$-projection. The composite $V\xrightarrow{r_V^{(b_2)}}B_{F_T^{b_2}}V\xrightarrow{r_{B_{F_T^{b_2}}V}^{(b_1)}}B_{F_T^{b_1}}B_{F_T^{b_2}}V$ has these projections $F_V^{b_1+b_2}$ and $v$, so is $r_V^{(b_1+b_2)}$, by [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Applying contravariant sections proves, under $H_T^{(b_1+b_2)}\cong H_T^{(b_2)}H_T^{(b_1)}$, the identity $d_T^{(b_1+b_2)}=d_T^{(b_2)}\circ H_T^{(b_2)}d_T^{(b_1)}$. Inverting gives $(d_T^{(b_1+b_2)})^{-1}=H_T^{(b_2)}((d_T^{(b_1)})^{-1})\circ(d_T^{(b_2)})^{-1}$. The Hom bijection of the composite adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] is the composite of its two Hom bijections. To compute this bijection explicitly, abbreviate $P_i=P_T^{(b_i)}$, $H_i=H_T^{(b_i)}$, $s_i=s_T^{(b_i)}$, $d_i=d_T^{(b_i)}$, with unit $\eta_i:\mathrm{id}\to H_iP_i$. The adjunct of $s_{2,N}\circ s_{1,P_2N}$ under $P_1P_2\dashv H_2H_1$ is $H_2H_1(s_{2,N})H_2H_1(s_{1,P_2N})H_2(\eta_{1,P_2N})\eta_{2,N}=H_2H_1(s_{2,N})H_2(d_{1,P_2N}^{-1})\eta_{2,N}=H_2(d_{1,N}^{-1})H_2(s_{2,N})\eta_{2,N}=H_2(d_{1,N}^{-1})d_{2,N}^{-1}$. These equalities use respectively the unit equation for $s_1$, naturality of $d_1^{-1}$, and the unit equation for $s_2$. Preceding this transformation by the canonical composition comparison, whose unit normalization was checked in Step 4, identifies this with its adjunct under $P_T^{(b_1+b_2)}\dashv H_T^{(b_1+b_2)}$. The unit equation and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identify it with $s_T^{(b_1+b_2)}$. This proves the addition law with the order of factors in the statement. The case where either exponent is zero uses the identity adjunction and the identity $r^{(0)}$; induction with $b_1=1$ gives the $b$-fold iterate.

proof.text: All module pullbacks in Steps 2--5 are exact and their derived pullbacks are induced termwise on complexes, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; no scheme-flatness assumption is required, since the coefficient maps are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Apply every $s$ and $c^0$ termwise. They commute with differentials by naturality, and the equalities of Steps 4 and 5 hold in each degree, hence on complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) these natural isomorphisms descend to the unbounded derived categories, and by (3) the equalities remain equalities of natural transformations there. The descended $s_T^{(b)}$ is exactly $\tau_T^{(b)}$ as defined in the item. The descended comparisons are the canonical composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]: both are natural isomorphisms between the same functors on $D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, and on a K-flat complex with flat terms both are the class of the termwise canonical isomorphism of module pullbacks (for the descended map by construction, for $c_{h,k}$ by its statement). Every complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ receives a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ from a K-flat complex with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], which is an isomorphism in the derived category; naturality of both transformations along it shows that they agree at $\mathcal G^\bullet$. Thus Step 4 gives $(\tau_X^{(b)}Lu^*)c_{u,b}=Lu^*\tau_Y^{(b)}$, and Step 5 gives exactly the asserted addition law. Every site and its module category uses the fixed small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so the localizations and adjunctions are on the stated categories.
